feat(slot): extend the pass past each end of a Slot

The Slot operation gets two parameters, extend_start (past A) and
extend_end (past B), in mm, zero by default. The pass runs past each
authored end by its own distance along the slot direction, so a slot can
run out through the edge of the face or edge that it was picked on.

The Slot's machine area is the stadium of the extended ends. The part law
does not change: the part section on a part source, and the setup's parts
on a stock source, judge the extended pass. An extension into a kept part
is a blocking Gouge, and the post refuses the program. The pick room
(#1504) still judges the authored slot.

The project file writes the keys only when they are not zero, and the
parameter digest appends them only when one is not zero. Thus earlier
slots keep their file text, stamp and output. The MCP edit_operation
patch reaches the fields through the Slot DTO.

fix(boundary): edges bound the cut - in any pick mode, and two edges keep the area between them

An armed Boundary row took the toolbar's pick kinds, so in Faces mode
no edge could be picked as a boundary. It now takes faces and edges in
any mode.

The open boundary may now hold two or more separate open chains: each
splits the stock as a single chain does, keeps the side holding the
operation's own area, and the area kept is between them - a face
bounded by two of its edges is faced between them and runs on at the
open ends. Chains that touch or cross, a chain with the area evenly on
both sides, a Contour given two chains and an include / exclude of
separate chains are each refused by name.

Fixes #1727

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(2d): two open edges are a band the stock outline closes (#1735)

A pocket-family selection (2D Offset, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive) of two
open part edges was refused as "an open run". The two edges are now
the walls of a band: band(e) = (side of A that holds B) ∩ (side of B
that holds A) ∩ (stock outline grown by the extension e). band(0) is
the selection's region; band(e) is a lane the area law clips its
extended result to, so the extension moves the open ends out of the
stock along the walls and the tool never rounds a wall end.

A selection with no clear band is refused by name (no stock, a wall
not level, two heights, not facing, touching or crossing walls, a
wedge, several pieces, more than two walls, mixed with closed
boundaries, containment On / Outside). One open edge keeps its old
refusal word for word. No gouge check is changed: a band pass that
cuts another part of the setup blocks the post.

Decision: docs/decisions/1735-open-edge-band.md

Fixes #1735

fix(3d): a whole-model 3D Pocket clears an open-sided notch past its edge

The 3D Pocket's footprint was the model's silhouette, and the level law
erodes it by the tool radius, so the cutter's edge never passed the
silhouette. A notch open to the part's outside kept a band one radius
wide, the full stock height tall, along its open edges, and the op read
ok; the next setup's fixture check then refused the post.

The source-built footprint of an untilted whole-model 3D Pocket (and of
Multi-Axis Rough, its stamped twin) now grows past the silhouette by the
tool radius less 0.01 mm (machining3d::open_sides), minus the setup's
other parts. The centre rides up to the silhouette edge where a level is
open; where a level's material is flush with the silhouette the band is
narrower than the erosion and cuts nothing. A picked or Boundary-
controlled region and a tilted plane keep the old reading.

Both kinds now read the setup's other parts in the solid law
(keep_law::neighbour_parts) as a second net, which also names a cut
through a part standing inside the model's own silhouette.

The #1706 pin on the as-imported sample (no tool fit inside a 6.53 mm
strip, so the op refused) now pins that the pocket clears beside the
strip and verifies clean.

fix(2d): cut an open Contour run on its air side

A Contour on an open run of a part rode the run on the tool centre, so
half the cutter cut the part the edge bounds (the gouge gate blocked the
post). The new machining2d::contour_open_run reads the part sections at
the cut levels, finds the side without material and offsets the run by
the tool radius plus stock to leave to that side. Material on both
sides, a side that changes, a tool that overlaps the part and a folding
offset are refused by name. A run with no material beside it keeps the
centreline ride. Side applies to closed rings only.

feat(sinker): compensate a Sinker Side Burn for electrode wear in Z

A Sinker Side Burn now takes a measured electrode wear and a layer
step. The plunge is burn_compensated's layered, wear-deepened plunge
under all of its refusals; the lateral move and its return run at the
last compensated tip, checked against the deepest-tip bound. The stock
sim reads the side burn as the worn electrode burns it. The by-name
refusals of a wear rate and a layer step on a side burn are removed; a
half-stated wear or a bad layer step is still refused by name.

feat(sim): carry machined stock into a setup turned side-on

A setup that stands the part on its edge (a quarter turn about X or Y
from the setup before it) now takes "what the setup before leaves
behind" as its stock. Until now the carry was refused by name.

- sim: `SideTurn`, `CarryTurn` and `Body::carry_side` (new module
  `stock_sim/carry_side.rs`). The level axis that stays level is
  re-indexed. The old heights become slabs of one cell, centred on the
  old Z range; a face inside a slab counts the slab whole. The old level
  axis becomes the height: the hull of the old column centres, each end
  moved out to the next centre that holds no material, or to the
  lattice edge. The carried body is never smaller than the body the
  columns hold, and at most one cell larger on a turned face.
- app: the program walk judges the body before a side-on turn and keeps
  those gouges for the final verdict (the hull can hide them), as a
  block left for a new block is kept (#320). The gate's note line says
  the stock was turned side-on.
- The rest chain, the prior plan and the carried block read the same
  `CarryTurn`; a lattice turn prints as before, so no stamp moves.
- The field engine refuses a side-on turn by name
  (`FIELD_SIDE_CARRY_REFUSAL`).
- `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL` has shorter words and now names the quarter
  turns; a turn off the quarter is still refused, naming the turn.

test(ui): pin the Bore ring plan in the detect-holes note tests

PR #1839 (#1566) lets Bore clear a wide hole with concentric rings, so
Detect holes keeps the Ø74.3 hole that the two UI tests expected it to
skip. The product is right and the tests were stale.

The tests now use a Ø10 bull-nose with a 4.999 mm corner. A Ø74.3
through hole is stored (14 rings). A Ø24 blind hole needs 8750 rings
at its flat floor, past the 4096 budget: it is skipped by name, and a
plate with only that hole is refused and stores nothing. The fixture
builder now takes a blind floor height per cell.

Fixes #1909
